brief: Anthropic met institutional investors in San Francisco on Oct 14 ahead of a possible IPO and will release updated financials. The market is fixated on one number, the annualized revenue run rate, because it will signal whether the IPO comes from strength or weakness. The focus follows OpenAI's revision last week from a roughly $70bn figure to about $50bn, which triggered an NDX selloff of 139bps before investors concluded the gap was gross-vs-net accounting rather than a real cut. Anthropic reports gross revenue while OpenAI reports net, so the same scrutiny now applies to Anthropic's own gross-based run rate, last disclosed at $65bn in July and reportedly on track for more than $100bn by year-end. Bulls want evidence that compute demand keeps accelerating despite falling token prices and new competing models from Meta and Google. Bears cite Anthropic's $42bn 2025 net loss, $518bn of mostly non-cancelable spending commitments over roughly a decade, widening hyperscaler credit spreads, and a $2.3tn industry backlog half owed by OpenAI and Anthropic. A hotter than expected CPI print this morning raised October rate-hike odds, lifting the cost of financing that spending just as $600bn of primary issuance and $1.7tn of lockup supply approach the market.
